new_statements.rule_in_words: Word-level prominence in (Apahapsili) Yali is a high/rising f0 target on the FINAL syllable of the phonological word; suffixes and enclitics count as part of the word, so the rise lands on the suffix/clitic syllable, never on the stem-final syllable before it (p. 7). The rise is clearest on phrase-medial words and is overridden phrase-finally by boundary tones (falls in statements). Duration shows no final vs non-final difference beyond phrase-final lengthening, so the authors tentatively conclude there is no word stress and classify Yali as a non-stress-accent language with a word-final, probably post-lexical, pitch accent; no lexical f0 contrasts are attested. For a position catalog: fixed word-final prominence, cued by f0 only.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None described; non-final syllables show lower/falling f0 (declination), with anticipatory lows on penults.
new_statements.exceptions: Phrase-final words: word-final rise replaced by boundary fall (or discourse-continuation rise); free grammatical function words (e.g. fam 'on/in') do not attract the rise, unlike suffixes/enclitics; six non-final-word final syllables with low falls were all creaky-voiced; the final rise is a strong trend (61% rises, 84% high-register contours on nf syllables) rather than exceptionless.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the phonological word / clitic group in connected spontaneous speech (not citation forms); authors leave open whether the rise belongs to the phonological word, clitic group or an accentual phrase. Study explicitly tentative ('first exploration'); whether word stress is truly absent is left for future work (vowel quality, spectral tilt untested).
new_statements.identity_note: The statement describes Apahapsili Yali (Glottolog dialect apah1238; DoReCo 'Yali (Apahapsili)'), which Glottolog/Ethnologue subsume under Pass Valley Yali [pass1247, iso yac] together with Landikma, Pass Valley proper and (per Fahner/Riesberg) Abenaho. The Riesberg 2021 sketch examined is attached to an Angguruk Yali dictionary (angg1239, iso yli) but uses Apahapsili examples; it is silent on stress either way.

sources.locator: p. 21 (Section 4, Discussion and conclusion); supporting description p. 7 (Section 1.2.5 Yali)
sources.note: Instrumental study of Apahapsili Yali spontaneous speech (30 speakers): word-final syllables (suffixes and enclitics count as word-final) carry a high/rising f0 target, clearest phrase-medially and overridden by phrase-final boundary falls; duration gives no evidence of stress, so the authors tentatively conclude Yali has no word stress but a word-final (probably post-lexical) pitch accent; no lexical f0 contrasts attested (pp. 7-9, 19-21).
